title: Today in one sentence
text: US stocks open at 9:30 am Eastern, and the prices here are Monday's close; the thing to watch is whether chip companies keep sliding (TSMC -2.0%, AMD -2.3%, NVIDIA -1.3% on Monday) while Meta (+3.4%) and Microsoft (+1.1%) held up, with inflation numbers due Wednesday and TSMC's report due Thursday.

title: TSMC reports on Thursday
text: TSMC makes chips for NVIDIA, AMD and Broadcom, so investors treat its report card as a clue about the whole AI chip business. TSMC says it will share its results on Thursday, Oct. 15 (2:00 am Eastern time). It closed Monday at $444.35, about 9% below its highest price of the past year ($487.47). Big reports can move a stock a lot in either direction.

title: Inflation report on Wednesday
text: The September inflation report (how fast prices are rising) is due Wednesday, Oct. 14. One analyst preview expects prices to be up about 3.6% from a year ago, compared with 3.4% in August. That is only a forecast. Higher inflation can keep interest rates high, and the Fed meets Oct. 27 to 28. Expensive-looking stocks tend to feel rate worries the most.

title: AMD is still near its target
text: AMD fell 2.3% to $594.24, but the experts' average guess for its price in a year is $607.59, only 2% higher. AMD is also a roller coaster stock (beta 2.5, so it tends to move about two and a half times as much as the market). Its price can swing a lot in either direction.

title: Rocket Lab had the biggest drop
text: Rocket Lab fell 3.7% to $65.71 on Monday, the biggest drop on our list. It is still about 56% below its highest price of the past year ($151). That shows how wild a small, fast-growing company can be: it also has the highest risk score on our list (9.9 out of 10).

title: Lesson 4: What is diversification?
text: Diversification means not putting all your eggs in one basket. On Monday, chip stocks fell (TSMC -2.0%, NVIDIA -1.3%) while Meta rose 3.4% and Microsoft rose 1.1%. If you owned only chip companies, you felt the whole drop. If you owned a mix, the ups and downs partly cancelled out. A fund like SPY holds about 500 companies at once, which is diversification in one purchase. It does not remove risk, and a mix can still go down when the whole market falls, but it can make the ride smoother.

title: What we could and could not check
text: Prices, 52-week ranges and expert price targets come from FMP, and prices are Monday's close. Experts' targets and company numbers were not available for Broadcom, Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Eli Lilly and Intuitive Surgical, so those spots are empty. The inflation forecast comes from one analyst preview, not from the government. Government and company websites could not be opened today, so the TSMC date was confirmed through search results that point to TSMC's own page. This is information to learn from, not advice to buy or sell.
